newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Mighty Dow rebound seen on shaky ground.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Mighty Dow rebound seen on shaky ground.

text.p: The Dow industrials' high-powered rebound is being built on shaky ground, lacking support from broad sectors of the market, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
A rebound in the Dow to fresh record highs that left the rest of the market behind would set up stocks for a new, perhaps harsher round of selling, they said.
"The worst possible thing, in my opinion, would be for the Dow to make straight up new highs here," said Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond James.
The Dow industrials were up 155 points, or two percent, to 6794 in late Tuesday afternoon trading. But the Nasdaq composite rose only three points, or 0.3 percent, to 1207.

Market breadth, as measured by the New York Stock Exchange's advance/decline line, also did not back the Dow rally, the technicians said. Advancing issues led decliners by a narrow seven-to-five ratio.

"I'm somewhat suspicious of the sustainability of this rally in the Dow," said Gregory Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "We're still in woeful shape in terms of breadth. This recovery still is extremely focused on the Dow."

With Tuesday's rally the Dow has recovered about 400 points of the decline that dropped the blue chip gauge to its near-term closing low of 6392 on April 11 from its record closing high of 7085 on March 11.
The Nasdaq composite, meanwhile, is barely above its recent closing low set April 2 at 1201. Its record closing high is 1388, set on January 22.
Bloch predicted the stock market would tumble 15 to 20 percent "if we get another (Dow) run to new highs unconfirmed by Nasdaq, unconfirmed by breadth."
The Nasdaq composite index bounced above the critical 1200 level in afternoon trading on Tuesday after dropping to a session low of 1194.
Technical analysts said that if the index were to close below the 1200 mark, its next line of support would be around 1150.

Nasdaq stocks could be trying to find a base around the 1200 level, the analysts said. And key to Nasdaq's holding the support levels is the performance of index heavyweights Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp.
"If Intel and Microsoft hold up, it probably won't (break 1200), because they're such a big part of that index," said Gary Kaltbaum at J.W. Charles.
Peter Green, vice president technical research Gruntal & Co said Microsoft had resistance at the 112 level and could move to 120 if that level were breached. It was up two at 109-5/8 on Tuesday.
Green said he saw resistance for Intel at 142, after which the stock could move to 150. It was up 1-1/8 to 139-1/2.
But gains by Microsoft and Intel, while propping up the Nasdaq composite, still hide heavy damage being done to individual Nasdaq stocks, Kaltbaum said.
"Unless the soldiers move with the generals, I don't know what kind of legs" the rebound rally will have, he said.
